preconditions.description: The number of students n is between 1 and 1000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= p_i <= n for p_i in p_list)
preconditions.description: Each p_i in the list p_list is a valid student number between 1 and n inclusive.
The list p_list contains exactly n integers corresponding to the n students.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= result_a <= n for result_a in result_list)
postconditions.description: Each result in the output list result_list is a valid student number between 1 and n inclusive.
The output list result_list contains exactly n integers, one for each student from 1 to n.

postconditions.expression: all(result_list[a-1] == find_double_hole(a, p_list) for a in range(1, n+1))
postconditions.description: For each student a (1-based), result_list[a-1] is the student who receives the second hole if a is the first student caught. The function find_double_hole(a, p_list) simulates the process starting at a and returns the student with the second hole.
